title: The double-dual morphism under a proper push-forward
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of separated finite-type
schemes over a field, and use finite coefficients invertible there.
On the ambient etale derived categories let
$\omega_T=Ra_T^{\times}A$ and
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_T)$. For every complex $K$,
the ambient exchange $D_YRf_*\cong Rf_*D_X$ identifies
$Rf_*\delta_K$ with $\delta_{Rf_*K}$. In particular, if the
latter is an isomorphism then so is the former.
Neither exceptional-adjoint admissibility on a constructible
subcategory nor geometric biduality is assumed.

proof.text: Use the ordinary unbounded small-etale module categories throughout. Write $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_T:T\to s$, $F=Rf_*$ and $H=f^{-1}$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes the finite-type $k$-schemes locally Noetherian; their finite affine covers, part of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], make them Noetherian. The structure maps are compactifiable by [def-asd-compactifiable]; $f$ has compactification $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$. For every chosen compactification $T\hookrightarrow\overline T\to B$ here, the proper map $\overline T\to B$ is finite type. Applying the same locally-Noetherian theorem over the Noetherian base $B$, and taking finite affine covers over a finite affine cover of $B$, also makes $\overline T$ Noetherian. Thus [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies all three ambient right adjoints, and [def-amb-etale-compact-support] identifies $Rf_!$ with $F$ on that proper model. Apply [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition] to $g=a_Y$ to obtain $Ra_{Y,!}F\cong Ra_{X,!}$ on the whole unbounded category. This is the needed left-adjoint composition, rather than a bounded-below composition used outside its domain.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; Stacks 0F7H–0F7J, ordinary torsion-ring unbounded specialization

proof.text:
The adjunctions in Step 1 give, naturally in a test complex $P$ on $X$ and $B$ on $s$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,f^\times a_Y^\times B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(FP,a_Y^\times B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{Y,!}FP,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,a_X^\times B).$$
For completeness, a natural family of bijections $\Phi_P:\operatorname{Hom}(P,U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,V)$ gives inverse arrows $\Phi_U(1_U):U\to V$ and $\Phi_V^{-1}(1_V):V\to U$: naturality says both families are postcomposition with these arrows, and the inverse-family identities give their two composites equal to identities. Applied here at $B=A_s$, it identifies $f^\times\omega_Y$ with $\omega_X$. Transport the counit of $F\dashv f^\times$ along this identification and call it $t:F\omega_X\to\omega_Y$. The construction uses only the three stated ambient adjunctions and the composition of Step 1, without a constructible exceptional-adjoint hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: composition of right adjoints

proof.text:
We will use the tensor–Hom adjunction on arbitrary complexes, with no perfectness condition. The first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], applied to the constant ring sheaf $A_T$, give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,R\mathcal Hom(L,N))\cong H^0(T_{\mathrm{et}},R\mathcal Hom(Q,R\mathcal Hom(L,N)))\cong H^0(T_{\mathrm{et}},R\mathcal Hom(Q\otimes^L L,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q\otimes^L L,N).$$
Here $H^0(T_{\mathrm{et}},-)$ means zeroth hypercohomology, computed by global sections of a K-injective representative as in [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]; it is an abelian group, not a cohomology sheaf. Evaluation is the inverse transpose of the identity. Set $e_L:D_XL\otimes^L L\to\omega_X$ and $e'_V:D_YV\otimes^L V\to\omega_Y$. By [lem-weil-duality-pairing], $\delta_L$ is the transpose of $e_L\sigma_{L,D_XL}$, so the defining equation is
$$e_{D_XL}(\delta_L\otimes1_{D_XL})=e_L\sigma_{L,D_XL}.$$
The identical equation holds on $Y$. All symmetries below are those of [lem-kun-tensor-sym], with the signed symmetry fixed by [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs; Stacks 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom)

proof.text:
Let $\epsilon_U:HFU\to U$ be the counit of $H\dashv F$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Define $\mu_{U,V}:FU\otimes^L FV\to F(U\otimes^L V)$ as the adjoint of $\epsilon_U\otimes\epsilon_V$ after the monoidal identification [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Equivalently, it is the projection map $FU\otimes FV\to F(U\otimes HFV)$ followed by $F(1\otimes\epsilon_V)$: taking adjuncts gives $\epsilon_U\otimes\epsilon_V$ on both sides. Define
$$b_L=tF(e_L)\mu_{D_XL,L}:FD_XL\otimes FL\to\omega_Y,$$
and let $\theta_L:FD_XL\to D_YFL$ be its tensor-Hom transpose under Step 3.

source.place: Proof, first and second paragraphs: explicit canonical internal-adjunction mate

proof.text:
For arbitrary complexes $M$ on $X$ and $N$ on $Y$, put $G=f^\times$, $P=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,GN)$, let $e:P\otimes M\to GN$ be evaluation and $c_N:FGN\to N$ the exceptional counit, and let $\chi_{M,N}:FP\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Y(FM,N)$ be the canonical internal-adjunction isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] for the compactification $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ of Step 1, on which $Rf_!=F$. For this compactification the compact-support projection isomorphism of [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] is the proper projection isomorphism $\lambda_{Q,M}:Q\otimes FM\xrightarrow{\sim}F(HQ\otimes M)$ of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], because $j=\operatorname{id}_X$ makes its extension-by-zero identification the identity. Let $q:Q\to FP$. Its $H\dashv F$ adjunct is $\epsilon_P\circ Hq$, with the counit of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. By Step 3 the inverse tensor–Hom transpose of an arrow $r:HQ\to P$ is $e(r\otimes1_M)$: evaluation is the inverse transpose of $1_P$, and the bijection is natural in the first variable. Hence the transpose $p$ of $q$ in [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] is $e((\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes1_M)$, and that node says that the inverse tensor–Hom transpose of $\chi_{M,N}q$ is
$$c_N\,F(e)\,F((\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes1_M)\,\lambda_{Q,M}:Q\otimes FM\to N.$$

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: "The isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is exactly the adjoint of this pairing"

proof.text:
Compare the projection expression with $\mu$ through $H\dashv F$ adjuncts of maps $Q\otimes FM\to F(P\otimes M)$; the adjunct of $h$ is $\epsilon\circ Hh$, and adjunction is bijective. Apply [lem-amb-tensor-projection-adjunct] with $K=Q$, $E=M$ and $a=1_{FM}$, so that $a^\flat=\epsilon_M$. Its map $\pi_f(Q,M)=F(\sigma)\,\mathrm{PF}_f(M,Q)\,\sigma$ is the composite defining $\lambda_{Q,M}$ in [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. Hence the adjunct of $\lambda_{Q,M}$ is $(1_{HQ}\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{Q,FM}$, where $c$ is the inverse of the comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Put $g=(\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes1_M$. Counit naturality $\epsilon_{P\otimes M}HF(g)=g\,\epsilon_{HQ\otimes M}$ gives the adjunct of $F(g)\lambda_{Q,M}$ as $g(1\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{Q,FM}=((\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{Q,FM}$. By Step 4 the adjunct of $\mu_{P,M}$ is $(\epsilon_P\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{FP,FM}$. So the adjunct of $\mu_{P,M}(q\otimes1_{FM})$ is $(\epsilon_P\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{FP,FM}H(q\otimes1)=((\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes\epsilon_M)c_{Q,FM}$, by bifunctoriality of $c$. Therefore
$$F((\epsilon_P\circ Hq)\otimes1_M)\lambda_{Q,M}=\mu_{P,M}(q\otimes1_{FM}).$$

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: "The isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is exactly the adjoint of this pairing"

proof.text: Postcompose the identity of Step 6 with $c_NF(e)$ and insert it into Step 5: the inverse tensor–Hom transpose of $\chi_{M,N}q$ is $(c_NF(e)\mu_{P,M})(q\otimes1_{FM})$. Taking $Q=FP$ and $q=1_{FP}$ shows that $\chi_{M,N}$ is the tensor–Hom transpose of the pairing $c_NF(e)\mu_{P,M}:FP\otimes FM\to N$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: "The isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is exactly the adjoint of this pairing"

proof.text: Specialize Steps 5–7 to $M=L$ and $N=\omega_Y$. Step 2 identifies $G\omega_Y$ with $\omega_X$. Under this identification $P=D_XL$, the evaluation $e$ becomes $e_L$ (evaluation is natural in its second variable), and $c_N$ becomes the transported counit $t$. Consequently the pairing of Step 7 is $b_L$ of Step 4, and the canonical comparison $\chi_{L,\omega_Y}$ is its transpose $\theta_L$. By [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] this comparison is an isomorphism for arbitrary $L$; no biduality or constructibility hypothesis is used.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: "The isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] is exactly the adjoint of this pairing"

proof.text:
Here are the naturality and symmetry identities needed in the evaluation calculation, with their verification. For $u:U\to U'$ and $v:V\to V'$, counit naturality gives $\epsilon_{U'}HFu=u\epsilon_U$ and $\epsilon_{V'}HFv=v\epsilon_V$. Hence the adjoints of the two sides of
$$\mu_{U',V'}(Fu\otimes Fv)=F(u\otimes v)\mu_{U,V}$$
are both $(u\epsilon_U)\otimes(v\epsilon_V)$; the adjunction is injective. For the symmetry identity, the adjoints of the two sides of
$$\mu_{V,U}\sigma_{FU,FV}=F(\sigma_{U,V})\mu_{U,V}$$
are both $\sigma_{U,V}(\epsilon_U\otimes\epsilon_V)$, by naturality of the canonical signed tensor symmetry and the monoidal inverse image. These are the definition of $\mu$ in Step 4 and [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], [lem-kun-tensor-sym], not an additional coherence theorem. In bidegree $(p,q)$ both interchanges have the sign $(-1)^{pq}$ of [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: naturality of projection and tensor symmetry written out

proof.text:
Put $L=K$. We prove the well-typed identity
$$\theta_{D_XK}\,F\delta_K=D_Y(\theta_K)\,\delta_{FK}:FK\longrightarrow D_Y(FD_XK).$$
Under the tensor–Hom bijection of Step 3, the left side corresponds to the following pairing on $FK\otimes FD_XK$:
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{D_XK}(F\delta_K\otimes1)
&=tF(e_{D_XK})\mu_{D_XD_XK,D_XK}(F\delta_K\otimes1)\\
&=tF(e_{D_XK}(\delta_K\otimes1))\mu_{K,D_XK}\\
&=tF(e_K\sigma_{K,D_XK})\mu_{K,D_XK}\\
&=b_K\sigma_{FK,FD_XK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is Step 9 naturality, the third is the defining double-evaluation equation of Step 3, and the last is Step 9 symmetry. For the right side, contravariant internal Hom acts by precomposition, so its pairing is
$$e'_{D_YFK}(\delta_{FK}\otimes\theta_K)=e'_{FK}(\theta_K\otimes1_{FK})\sigma_{FK,FD_XK}=b_K\sigma_{FK,FD_XK}.$$
The first equality is the same defining double-evaluation equation on $Y$ followed by naturality of symmetry; the second is the definition of $\theta_K$. Both pairings are equal, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the stated identity. This supplies the two-transpose argument and its signs explicitly; no invertibility of either $\delta$ has been used.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: the double-transpose equality

proof.text:
Both $\theta_K$ and $\theta_{D_XK}$ are isomorphisms by Step 8, which was valid for arbitrary $L$. The contravariant functor $D_Y$ sends inverse pairs to inverse pairs, hence $D_Y(\theta_K)$ is invertible. Therefore
$$c_K=D_Y(\theta_K)^{-1}\theta_{D_XK}:FD_XD_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_YD_YFK$$
is the double-dual comparison, and Step 10 gives $c_KF\delta_K=\delta_{FK}$. If $\delta_{FK}$ is invertible, $F\delta_K=c_K^{-1}\delta_{FK}$ is invertible, with inverse $\delta_{FK}^{-1}c_K$. This proves precisely the claimed implication for the pushed-forward arrow, without claiming that $F$ reflects isomorphisms. None of the argument restricts to a constructible subcategory or invokes geometric biduality.

source.place: Proof, final displayed comparison and last assertion
